resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported. SPA (official Saudi Press Agency release on Aramco's $25bn strategic gas expansion) states the MGS phase-3 expansion adds 3.15 bscfd 'by 2028'; Blackridge project profile states construction began Q2 2024 with completion Q4 2028. Two independent sources, both verified with '2028'. Note the value represents expected operational/completion year (Q4 2028), not a pre-existing operating date.

Diameter 12,16,10,4 in supported. Blackridge profile (Package 13 / Riyadh cluster) states verbatim: 'Lay various diameter lateral pipelines (16-inch, 12-inch, 10-inch, 4-inch) in the Riyadh cluster (470km).' Verified live with substring '16-inch, 12-inch'. MEED reports the identical 16/12/10/4-inch, 470km Riyadh-cluster detail but is paywalled (not citable); DMS Projects lists the Package 13 Riyadh Cluster but gates the diameters behind login. Single publicly-verifiable strong source, hence medium. GEM's original current_ref (MEED) is a dead link.

StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea = Saudi Arabia supported. SPA (official release) and World Oil both describe the MGS-3 expansion as delivering gas to customers across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia; the segment (Riyadh cluster) is domestic Saudi. Both verified with 'Saudi Arabia'. Two independent sources.

Owner1=Aramco (100%) supported. The Master Gas System expansion is an Aramco-owned, Aramco-awarded project (EPC packages awarded by Aramco, executed in collaboration with the Ministry of Energy); contractors named (KPIL, L&T, etc.) are EPC executors, not owners. SPA verified with 'Master Gas System'; World Oil verified with 'Aramco'. Aramco's own press release corroborates (originaltimes out live but archived: https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.aramco.com/en/news-media/news/2024/aramcos-strategic-gas-expansion-progresses-with-25bn-contract-awards, 200 OK). Two+ independent sources.
